title: Central Asian Square-Hole Coinage Atlas
definition: Coinages participating in the Chinese-style square-hole cash tradition within Central Asia and related eastern inland regions, including physically perforated square-hole cash and unpierced or pseudo-aperture issues whose design/manufacture clearly derives from that tradition.

temporal_scope.historical_focus: Post-Han through pre-Qing Central Asian square-hole cash traditions, with boundary and disputed records retained for review.
temporal_scope.early_material_rule: Clearly early Han/Eastern Han or earlier material is normally related/reference material; borderline issue dates, later circulation, local imitation, or uncertain dating remain retained rather than bulk-hidden.
temporal_scope.late_material_rule: Clearly Qing-era and modern material is normally related/reference material; disputed dates, local survivals, imitations, and boundary cases remain retained rather than bulk-hidden.
temporal_scope.boundary_disputes: Retain original date text, normalized start/end when supported, confidence, source, and separate issue/circulation/find/hoard dates. No current main-corpus record is bulk-hidden solely by the legacy 221–1643 working bounds.

notes: A physical through-hole is not required when an unpierced/pseudo-aperture coin clearly belongs to the same cash-form tradition.
Post-cast drilled, suspension, decorative or unrelated holes do not qualify by themselves.

places: Zabulistan / Arachosia where cash-tradition evidence exists
Tarim Basin localities with explicit Central Asian cash-tradition evidence

geographic_scope.rule: Included in extended-zone statistics only with evidence of Central Asian production, find context, circulation, or explicit type relationship.
